title: Ostrevia (Japan): clean package insert
about: The 2019 format in an English practice rendering: header items, the boxed Warnings, contraindications with their reasons in brackets, and sections numbered 1 to 26 with the gaps kept.

fixed.approval: 10 mg: 30500AMX00101000; 25 mg: 30500AMX00102000. Initial marketing in Japan: May 2024
fixed.storage: Storage: store at room temperature. Shelf life: 36 months.
fixed.category: STRK1 inhibitor (fictional); agent for chronic hand eczema
fixed.regulatory: Powerful drug; Prescription drug (Caution: use only pursuant to the prescription of a physician, etc.)

blocks.text:
1.1 Serious infections, including tuberculosis and pneumonia, some fatal, and malignancies have been reported. Use only under a physician with sufficient knowledge and experience of the treatment of hand eczema and of this drug, after explaining its risks to the patient.
1.2 Before treatment, check for tuberculosis by interview, an interferon-gamma release assay or tuberculin test, and a chest X-ray. [See 2.2, 8.1, 9.1.1.]

items: 2.1 Patients with a history of hypersensitivity to any ingredient of this drug
2.2 Patients with serious infections, including active tuberculosis [Symptoms may worsen. See 1.1, 8.1, 9.1.1.]
2.3 Pregnant women or women who may be pregnant [See 9.5.]

rows: microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow)
microcrystalline cellulose, mannitol, croscarmellose sodium, magnesium stearate; film coat: hypromellose, titanium dioxide, macrogol (25 mg tablets also iron oxide yellow)

blocks.text: 10 mg: white, round, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "10" on the other.
25 mg: yellow, oval, film-coated tablets debossed "HR" on one side and "25" on the other.
Chronic hand eczema in adults that has not responded adequately to existing treatment
The usual adult dosage is 10 mg of lumiravostat administered orally once daily. The dose may be increased to 25 mg once daily depending on the patient’s condition.
8.1 Serious infections may occur. Monitor patients carefully and instruct them to contact a physician promptly if fever, cough or fatigue occurs.
8.2 Measure lymphocyte and neutrophil counts, haemoglobin and liver enzymes before treatment, at 4 weeks and every 3 months thereafter.

sections.title: PRECAUTIONS CONCERNING PATIENTS WITH SPECIFIC BACKGROUNDS

subs.title: Patients with Complication or History of Diseases, etc.

blocks.text: 9.1.1 Patients with a history of tuberculosis or with findings suggesting tuberculosis: tuberculosis may reactivate.
9.1.2 Patients with risk factors for venous thromboembolism.
9.3.1 Patients with severe hepatic impairment: not studied; administration is not recommended.
Instruct women of childbearing potential to use effective contraception during treatment and for 4 weeks after the last dose.
Do not administer. Embryo-fetal toxicity was observed in rats and rabbits.
Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for 4 days after the last dose.
No clinical studies have been conducted in children.
Administer with care while monitoring the patient. Infections occurred more often in elderly patients.
Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.
The following adverse reactions may occur. Patients should be carefully monitored, and if any abnormalities are observed, appropriate measures such as discontinuation should be taken.
11.1.1 Serious infections (pneumonia 0.8%, herpes zoster 3.1%, tuberculosis frequency unknown)
11.1.2 Venous thromboembolism (0.3%)
There is no specific antidote. Monitor the patient for signs of adverse reactions and give supportive treatment. Lumiravostat is not removed by haemodialysis to a meaningful extent.
Instruct patients to remove the tablet from the PTP sheet before taking it. Swallowing the PTP sheet may cause the sharp corners to injure the oesophageal mucosa.
Peak plasma concentrations are reached 1 to 2 hours after a dose. The half-life is about 16 hours. Lumiravostat is metabolised mainly by CYP3A4.

subs.title: Clinical Studies for Efficacy and Safety

blocks.text: In two 16-week placebo-controlled studies (fictional HANDS-1 and HANDS-2, 1,210 adults), 38% of patients on lumiravostat 25 mg and 31% on 10 mg reached clear or almost clear hands, against 12% on placebo.
Lumiravostat is a reversible inhibitor of the fictional STRK1 kinase, which signals downstream of several cytokines involved in skin inflammation.
Nonproprietary name: lumiravostat (JAN). Description: white to off-white powder, slightly soluble in water.
21.1 Develop and appropriately implement a risk management plan.
21.2 Conduct a post-marketing use-results survey of all patients until data from a set number of patients have been gathered.
OSTREVIA Tablets 10 mg: 28 tablets (14 tablets x 2, PTP). OSTREVIA Tablets 25 mg: 28 tablets (14 tablets x 2, PTP).
1) Internal report: HANDS-1 study (fictional). 2) Internal report: HANDS-2 study (fictional).

title: Ostrevia (Japan): find and fix the errors
about: 6 planted errors: a header item, unboxed warnings, a contraindication without its reason, a section that moved up a number, an empty subsection and a strength.
